summary: Burst-smoothing configuration mismatch causing elevated 5xx and degraded throughput for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Gramline Media is observing a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (~8-12% error rate) and degraded throughput (50-70% of expected tokens/sec) for their dedicated capacity pool in us-east during tenant ramps. Errors began ~2026-03-08 22:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Affects live traffic for Gramline's dedicated cluster (high business impact).
- Streaming sessions drop with 502/503 when autoscaler tries to absorb short bursts.
- Observed increased tail latency (>2s P95) and token throughput collapse.

Observed behaviour and suspects:
- Autoscaler backoff and prewarm mismatch with tenant burst-smoothing policy leads to many short-lived runtime handoffs.
- API gateway shows queued requests that then hit runtime which reports OOM or watchdog restarts in logs.
- Prefix KV cache thrash during frequent model fast-starts amplifies latency and causes hedged retries to escalate into 5xx waves.

Request: Please investigate routing, autoscaler prewarm parameters and burst-smoothing policy for this tenant. Provide mitigation path and customer-facing ETA for resolution.
timeline: 2026-03-08 22:35 UTC: Gramline reported intermittent 502s via the support portal.
2026-03-08 22:40 UTC: Customer traffic shows a ramp (short spikes every 30s).
2026-03-08 22:42 UTC: SRE observed apigw queuing and hedged retry amplification in trace samples.
2026-03-08 23:05 UTC: Initial mitigation — reduced tenant max concurrency (temporary) — small improvement in error rate.
2026-03-09 03:12 UTC: Runtime logs show repeated KVM cache eviction and GPU driver watchdog restarts coincident with short prewarm launches.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Support escalated to platform on-call and opened this ticket.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate the customer's traffic pattern: repeated short bursts (50-200 concurrent requests) every 20-40 seconds over 10 minutes.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: mismatch between burst-smoothing window and autoscaler prewarm leads to many partially warmed runtimes, increasing OOMs and cache misses.
Confirmed via flamegraphs/traces: high proportion of calls hit runtimes that had been up <10s, showing cold-KV misses and longer kernel selection paths.
Observed hedged retry pattern at apigw: client retry + apigw hedged + runtime restart -> retry amplification chain.
Autoscaler logs show prewarm failures for GPU warmup when multiple launches overlap (NVML resets observed).
Network metrics: no significant packet loss between apigw and runtime; connection latencies normal.
risks_and_followups: Risk: naive temporary throttling could degrade UX for legitimate short-burst customers.
Follow-up: review tenant burst-smoothing defaults and add guardrail preventing prewarm overlap for dedicated tenants.
Follow-up: add metric to alert when >20% of requests hit runtimes <15s uptime for a tenant.
Follow-up: coordinate with runtime team to harden NVML reset handling during rapid prewarm cycles.
comments: Support - Maya Chen (2026-03-09): Customer reports 10-12% 5xx rate during marketing spikes. They cannot reduce burst frequency without breaking user flows.
SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-09): Reproduced locally with a traffic generator. Confirmed rapid prewarm overlap and NVML reset pattern. Raising to platform on-call.
Runtime Eng - Priya Nair (2026-03-09): We see NVML resets correlated with concurrent prewarm launches. Investigating driver retry behavior in our runtime shim.
Customer Success - Javier Morales (2026-03-10): Informed customer of ongoing investigation; provided short-term workaround to cap burst concurrency per route. Customer accepted temporary cap.
SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-11): Implemented temporary service-side backoff on hedged retries for this tenant; error rate reduced to ~3-4%. Working on next actions.
mitigation_and_resolution:
Short-term: applied tenant-specific hedged-retry backoff and reduced parallel prewarm concurrency. This dropped 5xx from ~10% to ~3.5% and restored throughput to ~85% of normal.

Next steps: finalize config change to burst-smoothing defaults for dedicated tenants, add prewarm overlap guardrail, and land runtime NVML reset hardening patch. Estimated ETA for permanent fix: 2026-03-16.

Customer-facing note prepared: apologizing for impact, explanation of temporary cap and ETA for fix.
